newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, Podravka forges ahead.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, Podravka forges ahead.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended mixed in slower trade on Tuesday with food firm Podravka forging ahead after news that it has made good progress in restructuring.
Market watchers expected the bull run to last in the weeks ahead although blue chips drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka, that set the market trend, dipped slightly at close.
They said good profit expectations for these leading firms would continue to provide enough investor incentive.
"I cannot see an end to the current expansion. It is like elsewhere in the world," said Velimir Zelimorski of brokerage Fima.
Six of 13 active stocks rose, four fell and three ended flat. Volume was lower at 20,937 units and turnover shrank to 7.4 million kuna from last Friday's 12.5 million.
Top gainer was Podravka, rising 57 kuna to 375 and was the most active issue with 11,303 shares sold. It hit an all-time record of 400 kuna in a last two-hour hike, traders said.
Podravka's stock has gained over 62 percent since the year start. The company said earlier on Tuesday it had got rid of five loss-making subsidiaries to consolidate its finances.
"That's what I've put my money on lately. It is too good a company to allow losers to drag it down," Zelimorski said.
He described a slow 15-kuna rise to 465 kuna of the chocolate maker Kras as "one of the biggest disappointments".

Kras was among the fastest rising stocks in 1996 on rumours it might follow in the steps of Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka by issuing Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) to improve liquidity, and listing them abroad.
But the company has so far failed to secure vital equity investment that would make it more than 50-percent private.
Hotel issues Laguna, Jadranturist and Istraturist continued to firm as buyers banked on these tourist firms in the northern Istrian peninsula attracting even more tourists this summer.
Laguna added 8.24 percent to 1,353 kuna on a volume of 329.
Zagrebacka's preference E-stock led decliners, falling 50 kuna or 5.0 percent to end at 950 kuna with 313 units sold.
Pliva lost 2.53 percent to 500 kuna on a volume of 1,641 shares after its 1/5 GDRs also traded lower in London.

Zagrebacka ordinary shares closed 1.07 percent weaker at 1,850 kuna with 99 shares sold after peaking at a historic 2,000-kuna high during the session. Its GDRs, issued at 10 to each share, fetched $32.5 on Seaq International.
